title: Roman missal states: bounded book and component revisions

traditions.label: Roman-curial missal and ceremonial witnesses
traditions.scope: Latin curial books and bounded ceremonial components before the 1570 Roman Missal revision.
traditions.coverage_note: An attested printed witness does not establish a direct ancestor of the 1570 recension.

traditions.label: Roman Missal: 1570–1962 editions and later supplements
traditions.scope: The 1570 recension and its later revisions, with bounded nineteenth-century corrections, complementary Holy Week books and the 1962 Canon amendment. The 2020 optional-preface and saints provisions are separately bounded.
traditions.coverage_note: Intervening calendar, rubrical and printed states are incomplete; no century-long identical text is inferred.

traditions.label: Postconciliar Latin Roman Missal
traditions.scope: Original Latin reform and typical-edition states, with companion lectionary distinguished from the altar book.
traditions.coverage_note: Independent vernacular histories are deferred. 1969 legislation, 1970 complete book and 2000 approval/2002 printing retain separate roles.

sources.title: Lippe, Missale Romanum Mediolani 1474, volume I (1899)
sources.inspection: Read rendered PDF 11 (preface), 15 (introduction ix), 35 (edited opening p 1); inspected explanatory text PDF 13–15.
sources.limitations: A critical edition, not direct examination of the 1474 copy; editorial additions and supplied lacunae are distinguishable.

sources.title: Legg, Tracts on the Mass (1904)
sources.inspection: Read page images of printed xxvi–xxvii, PDF 34–35, identifying 1501 and 1502 recensions and concrete expansion; earlier review read comparative notes 249–250.
sources.limitations: Scholarly comparison, not new full collation. Do not repeat the outdated claim that 1502 was the first standalone edition.

sources.title: Maura O’Carroll, Dominican Liturgy in the Thirteenth Century (1979)
sources.inspection: Previously inspected rendered article pp 80–84 and pericope comparisons in this research lane; cites Haymo presentation 1243 and critical editions.
sources.limitations: Exact Haymo manuscript-state and implementation remain unestablished here.

sources.title: Pałęcki, Carthusian Mass comparison (2015)
sources.inspection: Previously inspected printed 114 n 22 and 120–122; exact Rome 1570 Faletti/Varisco comparator and bounded Canon differences.
sources.limitations: Scholarly comparison, not new full collation. The exact original Rome 1570 copy has now separately been acquired and inspected at named loci; that does not independently reproduce every comparison in the article.

sources.title: Missale Romanum, Rome: Typographia Vaticana 1604
sources.inspection: Downloaded original scan for research; page images PDF 5 title, 9 Cum sanctissimum and 357 (printed 259, Ordo Missae final blessing) read.
sources.limitations: Google digitization used for research; no new retained-publication permission inferred here. One final-blessing rubric checked against the actual Rome 1570 Ordo and separately distinguished from Venice 1570; the constitution supplies correction policy, not an exhaustive before/after apparatus.

sources.title: Urban VIII, Si quid est (1634), reprinted in 1962 missal
sources.inspection: Read page image PDF 6: revision description and 2 September 1634 dateline.
sources.limitations: Later facsimile witness of the act; original Rome 1634 book not examined. A bounded 19 October 2026 search located Barcelona’s bibliographic entry for Rome 1634 and Madrid’s separate Antwerp 1634 record without a digital object, not a usable Rome scan. No 1604/1634 full-text comparison is claimed.

sources.title: Decretum approbationis editionis typicae Vaticanae (1920), in 2004 reprint
sources.inspection: Read rendered PDF 3, printed 3*, including 1900 baseline, appendix and 25 July 1920 dateline.
sources.limitations: This is the identified 2004 Bonn Aedibus Palmarum reimpressio, not an original 1920 printing. Its bibliographic identity is canonical; no proof all body readings equal 1920.

sources.title: AAS 47 (1955): March rubrics act and November Holy Week decree
sources.inspection: Downloaded official PDF and read page images 838–841, including §§ 1–2 and 6–9. Additional 2026-10-20 complete image inspection: De rubricis ad simpliciorem formam redigendis, pp. 218–224, with p. 225 next-issue boundary; dated 23 March 1955, effective 1 January 1956. Five titles include the Missal prescriptions at p. 224.
sources.limitations: Describes prescribed Holy Week state and effective date; complete 1956 service book not transcribed or page-collated here.

sources.title: John XXIII, Rubricarum instructum (25 July 1960)
sources.inspection: Read official Latin HTML, especially numbered 1–6 and dateline.
sources.limitations: Approves/replaces rubrical corpus; individual rubrical differences require code comparison.

sources.title: Missale Romanum 1962: June decree and later amended Canon in the available Vatican facsimile
sources.inspection: Read decree image PDF 2 and front-matter headings via text locator; source identity is existing canonical Vatican facsimile, not Benziger. Rendered printed p. 302/PDF 383 also inspected: the Communicantes already includes Joseph.
sources.limitations: Decree itself prints 23 July 1960 when referring to Rubricarum instructum; official act is 25 July. No silent correction. June book and later Canon amendment separated. This digital witness’s Canon is consequently not an unchanged June 1962 body; its retained June decree attests that earlier approval, while its body witnesses the subsequent amendment. Exact impression date remains unestablished.

sources.title: SCR, De S.Ioseph nomine Canoni Missae inserendo, AAS 54 (1962) 873
sources.inspection: Read original official page image 873: 13 November decree, 8 December effective date, insertion and proper Communicantes rule.
sources.limitations: Amendment to a book state, not a separate complete missal printing.

sources.title: Paul VI, Missale Romanum (3 April 1969)
sources.inspection: Read official constitution, new Eucharistic Prayers, Order, readings, propers and 30 November 1969 effective clause.
sources.limitations: English official translation used for description of Latin reform, not copied as prayer text; no territorial implementation inference.

sources.title: Missale Romanum, editio typica tertia 2002, constituent decrees
sources.inspection: Downloaded existing identified secondary digitally typeset witness; page images PDF 2–3 read for 1975 and third-edition decrees; title/publication list and 1970 decree read in PDF text. Also inspected rendered PDF 370, Ordo Missae § 144, for the existing dismissal formula.
sources.limitations: Secondary reproduction, not original printed page scan. 2000 approval/decree and stated effective clause are not 2002 publication; no full modern body import.

sources.title: Notitiae 44 (2008) 503–504, reprint notice and variations
sources.inspection: Downloaded official PDF; read page images 49–50, printed 367–368, for status and bounded changes.
sources.limitations: Official contemporaneous notice/list, not complete 2008 altar book. Only named changes, no exhaustive text collation.

sources.title: Paternas vices: Latin decree dated 1 May 2013, published 19 June 2013
sources.inspection: Read original Latin section, especially Exinde and Circa textus paragraphs, dateline and bulletin publication header.
sources.limitations: Describes exact amendment; no complete 2013 altar-book impression examined.

sources.title: Quo magis: Latin decree and seven-preface annex
sources.inspection: Read Latin decree and all seven annex sections, including their use rubrics; official HTML.
sources.limitations: Supplementary texts, not a new complete missal; no modern prayer bodies imported.

sources.title: Official explanatory note on the seven additional prefaces
sources.inspection: Read paragraphs on optional use, four postconciliar sources, three formerly local prefaces, and retained earlier concessions.
sources.limitations: Official explanation of repertoire and scope; no exact donor-edition collation or claim of newly composed prayers.

sources.title: Missale Romanum, Venice: Joannes Variscus, heirs of Bartolomeo Faletti and associates, 1570
sources.inspection: Downloaded complete PDF; visually read PDF 643 colophon (Venetiis, M.D.LXX.) and PDF 40–41 Ritus servandus final blessing, especially PDF 41 left column final paragraph before De his quae omittuntur in missa pro defunctis.
sources.limitations: Venice printing, not the Rome editio princeps cited by Pałęcki. One final-blessing rubric compared with Rome 1604; no whole-book equivalence or full recension collation inferred. Scan used for research; no new publication permission inferred.

sources.title: Sacred Congregation of Rites, decree of 23 September 1860, reprinted in the 1889 Desclée missal
sources.inspection: Read the rendered decree on PDF 14 of the complete 1,008-page 1889 witness; the dateline and the separate 14 March 1861 printing order are visible. The whole exact PDF is registered as remote for measured size, with the decree-bearing page retained as a canonical image derivative.
sources.limitations: Later printing of the act, not an independently acquired 1860 book. The operative change concerns recitation, while the prayers remain printable.

sources.title: Decreta authentica Congregationis Sacrorum Rituum, volume III (Rome, 1900), decree 3421
sources.inspection: Read rendered PDF 92, printed 80, decree 3421 (formerly 5694), 25 May 1877; checked the volume title identifying 1900. Complete exact PDF retained in the canonical source library for offline inspection.
sources.limitations: The delivery filename says 1898; the inspected volume title says 1900. A response to Pustet’s questions during missal preparation, not evidence that every proposed correction was adopted or that a new complete typical edition appeared in 1877.

sources.title: Ordo Missae, Ritus servandus and De defectibus, editio typica (Vatican, 1965)
sources.inspection: Complete 73-page Latin scan acquired from the linked public share; image-read approval p 5 and opening §§ 1–2, p 7, against the 1962 Ritus III.6 (printed LV, PDF 57).
sources.limitations: The 27 January approval decree has no separate effective-date clause. A component book for insertion into missals, not a complete 1965 typical missal. Modern scan identified by canonical artifact metadata; no redistribution permission or full-text collation inferred.

sources.title: Variationes in Ordinem Hebdomadae sanctae inducendae (Vatican, 1965)
sources.inspection: Complete 24-page Latin scan acquired from the linked public share; image-read title, decree pp 5–6 and Good Friday prayers pp 20–22; compared seventh prayer with 1962 printed p 173, PDF 254.
sources.limitations: Only the seventh Good Friday prayer is collated here. Chrism Mass, oil rubrics and the remaining prayers are not fully collated. The decree makes the changes effective for Holy Week 1965.

sources.title: Variationes in Ordinem Missae inducendae, Notitiae 3, no. 30 (1967), pp 195–211
sources.inspection: Read official synoptic old/new page images at printed 198–199 and 210–211; separately checked the 18 May 1967 decree in the acquired 40-page Vatican booklet.
sources.limitations: Official synoptic excerpts establish the named changes; no full missal collation. The 4 May instruction, 18 May booklet decree and 29 June effective date are distinct.

sources.title: Prece eucharistica and Preces eucharisticae, Notitiae 4, no. 40 (1968), pp 156–179
sources.inspection: Read decree printed 156 (PDF 26), selection norms 157 (PDF 27), and prayer opening 168 (PDF 38), including the reference to Canon I in the existing missal and the start of Prayer II. Additional 2026-10-20 image inspection: final unpaginated PDF p. 80 advertisement identifies the separate 54-page booklet, initial selection norms, red/black liturgical printing and Gregorian melody.
sources.limitations: The official journal supplies the decree and prayer texts. The separate 54-page Vatican booklet, including its physical and musical contents, has not been acquired. Later 1969–1970 institution wording is not retrojected into 1968.

sources.title: Emendationes in primam reimpressionem Missalis Romani inductae, Notitiae 9, no. 79 (1973), pp 41–42
sources.inspection: Read rendered PDF 46–47, including title, reference to 1970 page numbers and the boundary before the separate Aliae variationes section.
sources.limitations: Official retrospective correction list, not the complete 1971 altar book. The following Aliae section includes later changes and is excluded from this 1971 state.

sources.title: Notitiae 21, nos. 228–229 (1985), bibliography of typical liturgical editions
sources.inspection: Read rendered PDF 46, printed 398: the first reprint is explicitly assigned to 1971, with reference to the 1973 emendation list.
sources.limitations: Establishes the reprint year, not its exact issue day or a full before/after text comparison.

sources.title: Decree 652/08/L, Notitiae 44, nos. 501–502 (2008), pp 175–176
sources.inspection: Read rendered PDF 49–50, printed 175–176: papal approval on 2 February, decree on 8 June, and the specific implementation clause for the Institutio Generalis variation.
sources.limitations: The 1 November 2008 mandatory date concerns the Institutio Generalis variation; it is not asserted for every reprint correction. Omission of children’s prayers from this Latin volume is not their universal abolition.

sources.title: Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith, Cum sanctissima (22 February 2020), Latin decree
sources.inspection: Read complete official Latin HTML, norms 1–8, dateline and annex, including the 19 March effective clause and 5 December 2019 approval.
sources.limitations: A historical optional provision for the 1962 use. The decree does not supply a complete new missal or the future proper-text Supplementum.

sources.title: Official explanatory note on Cum sanctissima (25 March 2020)
sources.inspection: Read the three-page official note, including the prior RGMR 302 c fourth-class limitation, extension to selected third-class days, and future Supplementum.
sources.limitations: The note describes the supplement as forthcoming at publication; later publication or approval of its complete text has not been verified here.

sources.title: Missale Romanum, Rome: heirs of Bartolomeo Faletti, Joannes Variscus and associates (1570), Dominican Digital Library copy
sources.inspection: Complete 339-position DjVu archive acquired; read rendered scan 004 title, 332 colophon (ROMAE, MDLXX), 014 Ritus final blessing and 174 printed 290–291 Ordo/Canon conclusion. Four inspected evidence openings are retained as canonical PNG derivatives. Original openings 169 right through 172 left, printed pp. 281–286, were separately image-read for the complete strict Canon constituent; their four exact DjVu members and a four-page full-resolution PDF derivative are retained.
sources.limitations: The original Roman copy is acquired and identified. The strict Canon on printed pp. 281–286 is independently collated as a selective reading transcription, including rubrics, headings and 25 printed crosses; it is not a diplomatic glyph or chant-note transcription. The rest of the missal is not completely transcribed. The 108,391,684-byte complete archive remains remote for measured size. Venice 1570 remains a distinct witness.

stages.summary: Reported chapter presentation of the Franciscan-curial ordinal.

stages.limitations: Exact component redaction, authorship and community implementation require further witness study.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Short Burchard ceremonial

stages.summary: Shorter Ordo Missae recension within a Roman missal.

evidence.claim: Exact printer/copy and shorter recension identified.

stages.limitations: Separate from 1501 Giunta; no claim of a universally promulgated whole-missal revision.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Expanded Burchard ceremonial
stages.scope: Standalone ceremonial component.
stages.witness_label: Rome 1502 Johann Besicken; BM C.52.d.14
stages.summary: Expanded Ordo Missae with substantial added directions.

evidence.claim: 1502 text expanded relative to 1501; explicit examples.

stages.label: Roman Missal revised under Pius V
stages.scope: The promulgated Roman recension, anchored to an identified Rome printing and a separately identified Venice printing for one rubric comparison.
stages.witness_label: Rome 1570, heirs of Bartolomeo Faletti, Joannes Variscus and associates; original Dominican Digital Library copy inspected
stages.summary: Roman Missal revised under Pius V with ordered ceremonial and Roman Canon.

evidence.claim: Identified 1570 book and Canon comparator.
Recites the Pian missal as the book being revised.
Title and dated colophon establish the original Rome 1570 imprint.

evidence.locus: Scan 174, printed 291, right column after Placeat
evidence.claim: The Rome 1570 Ordo has a short instruction to bless the people and the formula; it does not contain the later explicit single/solemn/pontifical distinction at this locus.

evidence.locus: Original archive openings 169 right–172 left, printed pp. 281–286; retained four-page Canon facsimile PDF pages 1–4
evidence.claim: The complete strict Canon constituent is independently image-collated as 16 native selective-reading units with red headings, action rubrics and 25 printed crosses. This does not establish whole-Missal text coverage.

stages.limitations: The title and colophon identify the original Rome 1570 printing; 14 July Quo primum remains an act date, not its exact printing day. No full textual delta from 1474 is proven. The Ritus final-blessing directions differ from the separate Venice 1570 witness, so that witness cannot silently supply the Roman baseline. Exempt older uses are not incorporated. The native text binding completes only the strict Canon on printed pp. 281–286 under its declared reading normalization; the remainder of the wider running-head section and whole Missal remain untranscribed.
stages.reception: Roman use subject to Quo primum and its exemptions; no assertion that every Latin use was replaced.

stages.label: Clementine corrected missal
stages.scope: Vatican recension documented by its actual title and prefatory explanation.
stages.witness_label: Rome, Ex Typographia Vaticana, MDCIIII
stages.summary: Revises the Pian book; the inspected Roman Ordo comparison expands the final-blessing rubric with explicit count and solemn/pontifical distinctions.

evidence.claim: Book identity and emendation rationale.

evidence.locus: Ordo Missae, printed 259; PDF 357 right column after Placeat
evidence.claim: One final blessing even at solemn Mass; pontifical Mass retains three blessings.

stages.limitations: 7 July 1604 approval is distinct from the imprint year. The final-blessing rubric is compared with the actual Rome 1570 Ordo; other corrections are described by the act, not enumerated line by line. No first introduction of the single blessing or wholesale new conformity of liturgical quotations to the Vulgate is inferred.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Urbanian corrected missal
stages.scope: Book recension described in its issuing constitution.
stages.witness_label: Missale Romanum ordered for publication under Urban VIII; original 1634 copy not inspected
stages.summary: Clarified/restored rubrics and correction of scriptural divergences against Vulgate.

evidence.claim: Names prior revisions and describes corrections.

stages.limitations: 2 September 1634 is approval/instrument date. Later reprint witnesses the description, not every 1634 reading; no original 1634 title-page check.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Imperial prayers cease to be recited
stages.scope: Bounded Holy Week recitation rule; no new complete book identified.
stages.witness_label: 1860 decree reprinted in the 1889 Desclée missal
stages.summary: Discontinues recitation of the imperial prayers while retaining them in print.

evidence.locus: PDF 14, decree of 23 September 1860 and printing instruction of 14 March 1861
evidence.claim: Imperial prayers in Good Friday and the Holy Saturday Exsultet cease to be recited, but must remain printed in new missals.

stages.limitations: Printed presence after 1860 is not evidence of continued authorized recitation. No uncollated 1634 → 1860 whole-book ancestry is asserted.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Roman provision or witness; actual uptake and present-day authorization are not inferred.

stages.label: Selected corrections for Pustet’s missal
stages.scope: Three bounded corrections in a response about a missal in preparation.
stages.witness_label: SCR decree 3421 in Decreta authentica III
stages.summary: Corrects a Secret’s pronoun and an epistle’s book heading; makes an existing Creed rule explicit in the proper.

evidence.locus: Printed 80, decree 3421, responses II, IV and VI
evidence.claim: Corrects the Seven Sorrows Secret and Boniface epistle heading; requires an explicit Creed rubric on 9 November because the general rule already required it.

stages.limitations: Response II changes suae to suo; VI changes the heading from Ecclesiasticus to Wisdom, without establishing a new pericope. Response IV does not newly institute the Creed. No exact resulting Pustet printing or complete 1884 typical book has been inspected.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Roman provision or witness; actual uptake and present-day authorization are not inferred.

stages.label: Missal revised under Pius X and Benedict XV
stages.scope: Identifiable typical-book state; exact original printing not acquired.
stages.witness_label: Vatican typical edition 1920, described by decree reproduced in 2004 Bonn reprint
stages.summary: 1900 baseline adapted to recent prescriptions and Breviary revisions; appendix of approved local Masses.

evidence.claim: 1900 baseline and specific appendix described; 25 July 1920 approval.

stages.limitations: Neither later composite nor 2004 reprint is an original 1920 impression. 1634 → 1920 is not a proven single transition; intervening editions and prescriptions remain gaps.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Reformed Holy Week component
stages.scope: Complementary Ordo Hebdomadae Sanctae Instauratus replacing Holy Week order within Roman usage.
stages.witness_label: Vatican typical restored Holy Week order specified by Maxima redemptionis
stages.summary: Triduum moved from morning observance to prescribed evening/afternoon/night times.

evidence.claim: Prescribes revised Ordo and 25 March 1956 commencement.

stages.limitations: Approval 16 November 1955; effective 25 March 1956. Not an entire 1955/1956 Missale Romanum. Exact service-book printing and full prayer changes need inspection.
stages.reception: Roman rite follows revised Ordo; other Latin rites bound by celebration times only, per § 1.

stages.label: Canon with St Joseph inserted
stages.scope: Single amendment to 1962 Canon, including proper Communicantes forms.
stages.witness_label: 1962 Missal amended by De S.Ioseph nomine Canoni Missae inserendo
stages.summary: St Joseph is named after the Blessed Virgin before the Apostles in Communicantes.

evidence.claim: Exact insertion, extension and 8 December effective date.
The inspected facsimile body contains Joseph at the location prescribed by the November decree; its exact impression date is not established.

stages.limitations: Decree 13 November 1962, effective 8 December 1962. Not a separately identified complete printing; no new full Canon transcription. The inspected facsimile confirms the amended reading, but is not dated precisely enough to establish when that particular impression appeared.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Typical missal with new rubrical code
stages.scope: Whole missal accommodating 1960 code; Holy Week reform is a component.
stages.witness_label: June 1962 typical-book state attested by its decree, retained in the available later-amended Vatican facsimile
stages.summary: New general and missal rubrics replace older front-matter code and additions.

evidence.claim: New edition explicitly accommodated to new code.
Code effective 1 January 1961; new editions replace old rubric sections.

stages.limitations: The June state is not automatically the later December Canon state. Holy Week incorporation is not a fresh full-book collation. Code approval on 25 July 1960 differs from the mistyped 23 July reference in the 1962 decree. No existing target-1962 text projection is bound to this specifically June state. The available facsimile already includes Joseph at printed p. 302/PDF 383, so it does not supply an unchanged June Canon witness.
stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.label: Holy Week component revision
stages.scope: Holy Week supplement; the documented textual comparison is the seventh Good Friday prayer.
stages.witness_label: Variationes in Ordinem Hebdomadae sanctae inducendae, Vatican 1965
stages.summary: Recasts the seventh Good Friday prayer for Christian unity.

evidence.claim: Effective in Holy Week 1965; the seventh prayer is recast for all brothers believing in Christ, with unity in faith and charity.

evidence.locus: Good Friday seventh solemn prayer, printed 173 / PDF 254
evidence.claim: The older invitation concerns heretics and schismatics returning to the Church’s unity.

stages.limitations: A 24-page supplement, not a full missal. The complete set of changed prayers, Chrism Mass and oil rubrics remains uncollated.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Roman provision or witness; actual uptake and present-day authorization are not inferred.

stages.label: Revised Order and rubrical corpus
stages.scope: Ordo Missae, Ritus servandus and De defectibus component book.
stages.witness_label: Vatican 1965 Ordo Missae, Ritus servandus and De defectibus
stages.summary: Revises the existing missal’s Order and rubrics; the checked opening omits Psalm Judica.

evidence.claim: Approves the revised component book; the opening proceeds from Introibo to Adiutorium and Confiteor without Psalm Judica.

evidence.locus: Ritus servandus III.6, printed LV / PDF 57
evidence.claim: The 1962 rubric includes Psalm Judica after the opening antiphon, with stated exceptions.

stages.limitations: A complete scan of this component book is available, but only named loci were collated. Its approval is distinct from the 7 March implementation of Inter Oecumenici; the January decree itself supplies no separate effective date.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Roman provision or witness; actual uptake and present-day authorization are not inferred.

stages.label: Further changes to the Order of Mass
stages.scope: Variationes supplement to the 1965 Order; selected Canon and concluding rubrics.
stages.witness_label: Vatican 1967 Variationes and official Notitiae synopsis
stages.summary: Permits an audible Canon in Mass with the people, reduces ritual gestures, and places the blessing before dismissal.

evidence.claim: Synoptic columns show audible Canon permission, reduced gestures and changed concluding placement of the blessing, dismissal and Placeat.

stages.limitations: The acquired 40-page booklet is a supplement. The official old/new synopsis supports these loci without implying a complete new typical missal or any new Eucharistic Prayer.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Roman provision or witness; actual uptake and present-day authorization are not inferred.

stages.label: Three additional Eucharistic Prayers and prefaces
stages.scope: Repertoire and selection norms preceding the 1969–1970 complete missal reform.
stages.witness_label: Preces eucharisticae et praefationes, evidenced by Notitiae 40
stages.summary: Adds Eucharistic Prayers II–IV alongside the Roman Canon.

evidence.claim: Decree adds three Eucharistic Prayers and prefaces from 15 August; norms retain Canon I, whose text is referenced to the existing missal.

stages.limitations: Official journal text inspected; separate Vatican booklet remains missing. This is an expansion of options, not replacement of Canon I or proof of identity with the later 1970 prayer wording.
stages.reception: Historical Latin Roman provision or witness; actual uptake and present-day authorization are not inferred.

stages.label: Reformed Order and first complete typical missal
stages.date_label: 1970 complete typical missal; 1969 Order and reform separately dated
stages.scope: Complete 1970 altar-book state, incorporating the 1969 Order and reform; the complementary reading system remains distinguished.
stages.witness_label: Ordo Missae 1969 and Missale Romanum editio typica 1970; complementary publications in one reform state
stages.summary: Revised Order, expanded Eucharistic Prayer repertoire and seasonal propers; multi-year readings in companion system.

evidence.locus: PDF 1 title/publication list and Celebrationis eucharisticae
evidence.claim: 1970 complete typical edition; 26 March 1970 decree.

stages.limitations: Approval on 3 April 1969 and the reform’s effective date of 30 November 1969 are distinct from publication of the complete book in 1970. stages.reception: Latin Roman use; no claim that every local church used this exact printing.

stages.reception: Historical Latin Roman provision or witness; actual uptake and present-day authorization are not inferred.
